F2-MIRROR-LITERAL.rationale: Literal lookup matches value and metadata. Suffix lookup selects the distinct ratio. Unique-target lookup rejects the two destinations.

F2-MIRROR-SUFFIX.rationale: Suffix lookup matches the claim to the second value and its metadata. Literal lookup fails. Unique-target lookup rejects the two destinations.

F2-CONTEXT-SUFFIX.rationale: All three raw records are byte-identical to F2-MIRROR-LITERAL. A distinct synthetic context declares the suffix-local rule for its transcript adjudication.

F2-RFC-ESCAPE-ORDER.rationale: RFC 6901 transforms ~1 before ~0, so token ~01 denotes key ~1. The deliberately distinct value at key / exposes reversal of the decoding order.

F2-IDENTITY-CORRECT.rationale: The intended target preserves the value and cohort-a field metadata.

F2-IDENTITY-WRONG-TARGET.rationale: Both targets have value 73, but the changed pointer selects cohort-b and conflicts with the claim metadata for cohort-a.

F2-RFC-ARRAY-INDEX.rationale: Array index /1 resolves to the second element.

F2-RFC-ARRAY-PADDED.rationale: An array index with a leading zero violates RFC 6901. Matching field metadata is present so the expected failure is specifically resolution.

F2-RFC-OBJECT-PADDED.rationale: Object member 01 is a literal key and the array index restriction does not apply.

F2-MISSING-RESULT.rationale: R11 is absent. The claim syntax and metadata do not establish a conflict, but the referenced result cannot be verified.

direct_controls_underdetermined.rationale: The direct pointer and missing-evidence controls agree across every alias policy.

mirror_suffix_identifies_set.rationale: The alias claim agrees only with the suffix destination. Two policies remain because both select that destination in this case.

differing_local_rules_out_of_model.rationale: Independent manual assessments under the two declared local policies disagree on byte-identical raw evidence. No single global policy yields that transcript.
